name: Ritzman Animal Nutrition Lab
use: Animal nutrition research laboratory (COLSA/NHAES); current occupants not confirmed

facts.text: The lab was built in 1959 to replace the original nutrition laboratory in the creamery, which burned in 1956; it was dedicated in 1960.
It is named for Ernest G. Ritzman (1875–1955), who started UNH's animal metabolism research program in 1918 and continued work begun with a flock of sheep bequeathed by Alexander Graham Bell.

verdict: Plain 1959 painted-block lab with window air conditioners, built after the creamery fire; current use unknown.
notes: notunh's label 'Ritzman Labatory' is misspelled; the building is the Ritzman Animal Nutrition Lab or Ritzman Laboratory. Current use and occupants weren't found: COLSA's facilities list has no entry for it. The reference photo shows a plain two-story painted block building with window A/C units (so central A/C is unlikely), small awnings and a tired, utilitarian look. No licensed photo, no renovation record, no reviews.
